nodes.description: Biallelic nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, or small indel variants in PCNT (21q22.3) abolish production of functional pericentrin, an unusually large coiled-coil scaffold protein of the pericentriolar material. Sequence analysis detects the great majority of pathogenic alleles; missense variants are a minor contributor. Some individuals originally reported as having Seckel syndrome carry PCNT loss-of-function variants and are, on review, clinically compatible with MOPD II.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the pericentrin (PCNT) gene cause primordial dwarfism.
evidence.snippet: Using genetic linkage analysis, we find that biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the centrosomal pericentrin (PCNT) gene on chromosome 21q22.3 cause microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type II (MOPD II) in 25 patients.

evidence.snippet: It is therefore concluded that, despite variable severity, MOPDII is a genetically homogeneous condition due to loss-of-function of pericentrin.

nodes.description: Pericentrin anchors both structural and regulatory proteins at the centrosome, including gamma-tubulin ring complexes that nucleate spindle microtubules. Its absence disorganizes the mitotic spindle and causes chromosome missegregation in dividing cells. This node substitutes PCNT for the generic centrosome/spindle lesion of the neural progenitor centrosome-spindle module.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the pericentrin (PCNT) gene cause primordial dwarfism.
evidence.snippet: Absence of PCNT results in disorganized mitotic spindles and missegregation of chromosomes.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in pericentrin cause Seckel syndrome with defective ATR-dependent DNA damage signaling.
evidence.snippet: We now report that mutations in the gene encoding pericentrin (PCNT)--resulting in the loss of pericentrin from the centrosome, where it has key functions anchoring both structural and regulatory proteins--also cause Seckel syndrome.

nodes.description: Moyamoya disease is treated with extracranial-intracranial revascularization (usually indirect), and intracranial aneurysms with clipping or endovascular treatment. Surgery is technically demanding given patient size but is feasible at expert centers with good long-term outcomes.

evidence.reference_title: Surgical outcomes of Majewski osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism Type II with intracranial vascular anomalies.
evidence.snippet: Microneurosurgery with either intracranial bypass or aneurysm clipping is extremely challenging but feasible at expert centers in patients with MOPD II, and good long-term outcomes are possible.

nodes.description: Pericentrin loss also impairs ATR-dependent DNA damage checkpoint signaling, the same pathway disrupted by hypomorphic ATR variants in Seckel syndrome. This provides the first mechanistic link between a structural centrosomal protein and DNA damage signaling and explains why the centrosomal and DNA-damage-response classes of microcephalic primordial dwarfism converge on one clinical phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in pericentrin cause Seckel syndrome with defective ATR-dependent DNA damage signaling.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we find that cells of individuals with Seckel syndrome due to mutations in PCNT (PCNT-Seckel) have defects in ATR-dependent checkpoint signaling, providing the first evidence linking a structural centrosomal protein with DNA damage signaling.

nodes.description: Beyond the growth deficit, MOPD II carries a distinctive systemic vasculopathy affecting the intracranial, coronary, renal, and external carotid circulations. Neurovascular disease (moyamoya vasculopathy and intracranial aneurysms) is the leading cause of premature death; moyamoya tends to present earlier than aneurysms, and aneurysm risk persists across the shortened lifespan. Hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and premature coronary artery disease with myocardial infarction in young adults complete the picture. This is a parallel arm that is not fully explained by the proliferation deficit alone; the intervening cell biology is curated as an explicit knowledge gap rather than asserted.

nodes.description: Severe insulin resistance and early-onset diabetes are common in PCNT deficiency but are not congenital — they emerge during childhood and adolescence. Pericentrin knockdown in adipocytes does not impair proximal insulin signaling but does impair insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in proportion to a defect in cell proliferation and adipogenesis, suggesting partial failure of adipocyte differentiation rather than a receptor-proximal signaling lesion.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic defects in human pericentrin are associated with severe insulin resistance and diabetes.
evidence.snippet: Of 21 patients with genetic defects in PCNT, 18 had insulin resistance, which was severe in the majority of subjects.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic defects in human pericentrin are associated with severe insulin resistance and diabetes.
evidence.snippet: Knockdown of pericentrin in adipocytes had no effect on proximal insulin signaling but produced a twofold impairment in insulin-stimulated glucose uptake, approximately commensurate with an associated defect in cell proliferation and adipogenesis.

nodes.description: Intracranial aneurysms occur across childhood and adulthood and carry the risk of subarachnoid hemorrhage; ruptured aneurysm is a leading cause of death in this population.

nodes.description: Impaired mitotic fidelity and checkpoint signaling reduce the proliferative output of rapidly dividing progenitor pools during embryonic and fetal development — neural progenitors in the cortical germinal zones, and growth plate chondrocytes and osteoblasts in the skeleton. Because the lesion is in a ubiquitously required mitotic apparatus rather than a tissue-restricted program, the deficit is global rather than organ-selective, which is what makes the resulting growth failure "primordial" (prenatal in onset and never caught up).
